decoded.meaning: NAME{"conn"} — RFC-0014 §2/§3 `remove-reserved-rejected`: the endpoint cannot be made to remove itself; the write is REFUSED and never routes to retire()
decoded.note: `conn` is a reserved, protocol-owned name per module. The refusal is the registered identity `tr::access::denied` (0x0050) — the wire code the reference implementation's status_t::PERMISSION_DENIED maps to (core/src/fwd_reply.cpp). RFC-0014 §2 spells this `tr::acl::permission_denied`, which is NOT a registered identity in RFC-0002 §D's table; the registered spelling is `tr::access::denied`. Under RFC-0014 §Discussion's clause-kind rule the error identity is pinned by code PLUS this vector, so 0x0050 is what a conformant peer reads and the RFC's spelling is an erratum, not a second code.
